```{r}
library(dada2); packageVersion("dada2")
```


```{r}
path <- "/home/rstudio/Dada2/Dada2/MiSeq_SOP" # CHANGE ME to the directory containing the fastq files after unzipping.
list.files(path)
```
The following chunk takes the raw sequencing files, separating F1 (forward) and R2 (reverse) sequences. Then, the sample names are extracted from the file names.
```{r}
# Separate forward (R1) and reverse (R2) reads and extract sample names from filenames
fnFs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern="_R1_001.fastq", full.names = TRUE))
fnRs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern="_R2_001.fastq", full.names = TRUE))
# Extract sample names, assuming filenames have format: SAMPLENAME_XXX.fastq
sample.names <- sapply(strsplit(basename(fnFs), "_"), `[`, 1)
```

The following chunk generates plots to visualise the quality of the raw sequence. This helps us determine at which sequencing cycle the auqlity decreases, so we can choose the proper truncation thresholds.
```{r}
# Plot sequence quality scores to determine where to truncate the reads
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[1:2])
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[1:2])
```
By looking at both graphs, we can see that the forward sequences have a high quality score (above 30) for the first 250 cycles. The reverse sequence, however, contains a significant decrease after cycle 160, which explains why we use truncLen=c(240, 160) during filtering.

The next chunk filters out poor-quality sequences. it trims them to a defined length, and removes undetermined bases and the PhiX genome.
```{r}
# Place filtered files in filtered/ subdirectory
filtFs <- file.path(path, "filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_F_filt.fastq.gz"))
filtRs <- file.path(path, "filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_R_filt.fastq.gz"))
names(filtFs) <- sample.names
names(filtRs) <- sample.names

# Filter reads based on quality (maxEE=2), remove Ns, and truncate forward reads to 240bp and reverse to 160bp
out <- filterAndTrim(fnFs, filtFs, fnRs, filtRs, truncLen=c(240,160),
              maxN=0, maxEE=c(2,2), truncQ=2, rm.phix=TRUE,
              compress=TRUE, multithread=FALSE) # On Windows set multithread=FALSE (only needed for filterAndTrim)
head(out)   
```

The next chunk is used to estimate the error profile specific to the sequencing run. It's essencial to ddistinguish true biological variants from sequencing errors.
```{r}
# Use machine learning to model the specific sequencing error rates of this run
errF <- learnErrors(filtFs, multithread=TRUE)
errR <- learnErrors(filtRs, multithread=TRUE)
plotErrors(errF, nominalQ=TRUE)
```

The graphs shows the modeled error rates (defined by the back lines) and track the observed error frequencies (points) for all base substitutions. As the consensus quality scores increase, the error rates decrease, which confirms that this is a well-fitted model.

The next chunk is usedapply the core sample inference algorithm to the filtered and trimmed sequence data, so we can identify the true Amplicon Sequence Variants.
```{r}
# Apply the core DADA2 algorithm to infer true biological sequences (ASVs) by correcting errors
dadaFs <- dada(filtFs, err=errF, multithread=TRUE)
dadaRs <- dada(filtRs, err=errR, multithread=TRUE)
```

```{r}
dadaFs[[1]]
```

The next chunk is used to merges the forward and reverse sequences so we can reconstruct the complete amplicon sequence based on their overlapping regions.
```{r}
# Merge overlapping forward and reverse denoised reads to reconstruct the full amplicon
mergers <- mergePairs(dadaFs, filtFs, dadaRs, filtRs, verbose=TRUE)
# Inspect the merger data.frame from the first sample
head(mergers[[1]])
```
The next chunk compiles the merged sequences into an abundance matriix to show how many times each variant appears in each sample.
```{r}
# Compile all merged sequences into a single ASV abundance table
seqtab <- makeSequenceTable(mergers)
dim(seqtab)
# Inspect distribution of sequence lengths
table(nchar(getSequences(seqtab)))
```
The next chunk hemps used identify and remove chimeric sequences. Those sequences are artifical artifacts that are created during PCR.
```{r}
# Identify and remove chimeric sequences (PCR artifacts)
seqtab.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab, method="consensus", multithread=TRUE, verbose=TRUE)
dim(seqtab.nochim)
sum(seqtab.nochim)/sum(seqtab)
```
The results show us that 

The next chunk creates a summary table so we can verify the percentage of sequences successfully retained through the steps above.
```{r}
getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))
track <- cbind(out, sapply(dadaFs, getN), sapply(dadaRs, getN), sapply(mergers, getN), rowSums(seqtab.nochim))
# If processing a single sample, remove the sapply calls: e.g. replace sapply(dadaFs, getN) with getN(dadaFs)
colnames(track) <- c("input", "filtered", "denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nonchim")
rownames(track) <- sample.names
head(track)
```
The next few chunks are part of the taxonomic assignment, for the identified ASVs (starting at Kingdom, then Genus, and Species). It compares them to specific reference databases to be the most accurate possible.
```{r}
library(dada2)

# Assign taxonomy up to the Genus level
taxa <- assignTaxonomy(seqtab.nochim, "silva_nr99_v138.2_toGenus_trainset.fa.gz", multithread = TRUE)

# Vérifier les résultats
head(taxa)
```
```{r}
library(dada2)
# Add species-level assignment
taxa2 <- addSpecies(taxa, "silva_v138.2_assignSpecies.fa.gz")
head(taxa)
```
```{r}
taxa.print <- taxa # Removing sequence rownames for display only
rownames(taxa.print) <- NULL
head(taxa.print)
```

```{r}
library(DECIPHER); packageVersion("DECIPHER")
```
The next 2 chunks are used to evaluate the accuracy of the mock community. it contains 20 bacterial strains. When we run it, 20 ASVs exactly match the reference genomes of the expected community, which givese us a residual error rate after the DADA2 pipeline of 0% for the sample.
```{r}
unqs.mock <- seqtab.nochim["Mock",]
unqs.mock <- sort(unqs.mock[unqs.mock>0], decreasing=TRUE) # Drop ASVs absent in the Mock
cat("DADA2 inferred", length(unqs.mock), "sample sequences present in the Mock community.\n")
```
```{r}
mock.ref <- getSequences(file.path(path, "HMP_MOCK.v35.fasta"))
match.ref <- sum(sapply(names(unqs.mock), function(x) any(grepl(x, mock.ref))))
cat("Of those,", sum(match.ref), "were exact matches to the expected reference sequences.\n")
```

The rest of the analyse uses phyloseq
```{r}
#import into phyloseq
library(phyloseq); packageVersion("phyloseq")
```
```{r}
library(Biostrings); packageVersion("Biostrings")
```
```{r}
library(ggplot2); packageVersion("ggplot2")
```
```{r}
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

Firstly, we need to construct the Phyloseq object to analyse the ecological diversity. Phyloseq combines the sequence table, the taxonomy assignments, and the experimental metadata to create an unified data object.
```{r}
# Extract sample metadata from sample names
samples.out <- rownames(seqtab.nochim)
subject <- sapply(strsplit(samples.out, "D"), `[`, 1)
gender <- substr(subject,1,1)
subject <- substr(subject,2,999)
day <- as.integer(sapply(strsplit(samples.out, "D"), `[`, 2))

# Create sample metadata dataframe
samdf <- data.frame(Subject=subject, Gender=gender, Day=day)
samdf$When <- "Early"
samdf$When[samdf$Day>100] <- "Late"
rownames(samdf) <- samples.out

# Assemble the phyloseq object (ASV table + Taxonomy + Metadata)
ps <- phyloseq(otu_table(seqtab.nochim, taxa_are_rows=FALSE),
               sample_data(samdf),
               tax_table(taxa))
ps <- prune_samples(sample_names(ps) != "Mock", ps) # Remove mock sample

dna <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(taxa_names(ps))
names(dna) <- taxa_names(ps)
ps <- merge_phyloseq(ps, dna)
taxa_names(ps) <- paste0("ASV", seq(ntaxa(ps)))
ps
```

```{r}
# Plot Alpha Diversity metrics
plot_richness(ps, x="Day", measures=c("Shannon", "Simpson"), color="When")
```

```{r}
# Transform data to proportions as appropriate for Bray-Curtis distances
ps.prop <- transform_sample_counts(ps, function(otu) otu/sum(otu))
# Calculate Bray-Curtis distance matrix and run NMDS ordination
ord.nmds.bray <- ordinate(ps.prop, method="NMDS", distance="bray")
```
```{r}
# Visualize the NMDS ordination plot
plot_ordination(ps.prop, ord.nmds.bray, color="When", title="Bray NMDS")
```
```{r}
# Filter for the top 20 most abundant taxa
top20 <- names(sort(taxa_sums(ps), decreasing=TRUE))[1:20]
ps.top20 <- transform_sample_counts(ps, function(OTU) OTU/sum(OTU))
ps.top20 <- prune_taxa(top20, ps.top20)
# Plot relative abundance at the Family level
plot_bar(ps.top20, x="Day", fill="Family") + facet_wrap(~When, scales="free_x")
```
